R0217.title: XR Device Firmware Attack
R0217.definition: Attackers exploit firmware vulnerabilities in VR/AR headsets, controllers and other XR devices to achieve device control, data theft or malicious code implantation.

references.title: Legal risks in metaverse development: technology and data

R0217.description:
XR device firmware attacks target headsets, controllers, base stations, and sensor firmware. Attackers may exploit update mechanisms, driver flaws, or debug interfaces to control devices and steal visual, motion, or spatial data.

XR devices hold high privileges and collect sensitive body and environment signals. Vendors need firmware signing, permission isolation, vulnerability response, and peripheral trust controls.

Limitation: Requires device vulnerabilities and physical proximity
R0217.influence: XR firmware compromise can expose camera, motion, spatial, and sensor data while giving attackers control of high-privilege devices.

observables: XR device firmware update package signature verification is missing or bypassed
Device debug interfaces or drivers show traces of unauthorized access
Sensor views, motion, or spatial data are abnormally read or exfiltrated
The device peripheral trust chain shows unexpected device attachment
Firmware versions carry known vulnerabilities left unpatched
